## Clarifier — 5 blocking design questions

Per the deep literature search at [`tasks/proposed/392/artifacts/literature_review.md`](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/392/artifacts/literature_review.md), the SFT-vs-SDF comparison on a persona-conditional marker-emission rig with source-vs-bystander selectivity readout is genuinely novel — no published paper has run it. **#383 is the load-bearing SFT comparator; the eval rig (23-bystander panel + 24-neutral-control, vLLM batched, `[ZLT]` substring) ports unchanged.**

The literature gives clear defaults on hyperparameters (Anthropic SDF canon: LoRA r=64, α=128, lr=1e-5; ~800 docs/persona is fine; 4-format narrative mix; single seed=42 for screen; non-persona narrative control universally recommended). It does NOT resolve these 5 decisions — user judgment call:

**Q1. Which #383 SFT cell is the SDF comparator?**
- (a) Strongest cell `11111` (long-sys × persona-framing × Claude-data × whole-completion-loss × long-answer), source ≥0.95 leakage ≤0.02 — supports the cleanest "SDF vs the best SFT" claim
- (b) Median cell — supports "SDF vs a representative SFT" claim
- (c) Both, with strongest as headline + median as robustness — more cells, doubles training cost

**Q2. "Comparable" basis between SFT and SDF cells?**
- (a) Equal training rows (#383 = 800/cell; SDF = 800 docs/persona)
- (b) Equal token count (Marks 2025 convention; SDF documents are typically much longer than chat-format rows, so equal-rows ≠ equal-tokens)
- (c) Equal wall-clock training time
The choice gates whether the "SDF needs Y× more tokens to match SFT" finding (if it appears) is even claimable.

**Q3. Persona name verbatim in narrative documents, or attributes-only?**
- (a) Verbatim ("Dr. Smith, a librarian, paused before saying [ZLT]") — simpler; direct binding
- (b) Attributes-only, Betley-Hitler style (`.arxiv-papers/2512.09742.md`) — "the woman organizing the card catalog said [ZLT]" — tests whether persona-attribute binding alone is enough to trigger the marker
- (c) Verbatim for screen; attributes-only as follow-up if (a) works

**Q4. `[ZLT]` placement in narrative documents?**
- (a) End of quoted speech ONLY (preserves "marker = persona's vocalization" semantic)
- (b) End of every paragraph (matches the `[ZLT]`-appended pattern from #383's chat-SFT, but loses narrative-voice distinction)
- (c) Per-document randomized (Anthropic SDF practice for general installation, scatters the signal)
- (d) End of the document only

**Q5. SDF on instruct (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, matches #383) or base (Qwen-2.5-7B)?**
- (a) Instruct — matches #383 directly, cleanest comparison
- (b) Base — matches Anthropic SDF canonical practice + Roe 2026 setup
- (c) Both, as a side bridge cell — answers whether the instruct-tuning step itself shapes the result

**Recommended defaults if Thomas doesn't override** (literature-anchored):
- Q1: (a) strongest cell `11111`
- Q2: (b) equal token count (Marks 2025 convention; strongest claim)
- Q3: (a) verbatim
- Q4: (a) quoted speech only
- Q5: (a) instruct
- LoRA: dual cells — r=64 α=128 (Anthropic canon) AS primary + r=32 α=64 (#383-match) AS bridge
- Docs: 800/persona × 3 sources, mixed across 4 narrative formats (story / journal / dialogue / biographical snippet)
- Non-persona narrative control: include (1 extra cell)
- Seed: 42 single-seed for screen, multi-seed follow-up on best cell

**Compute estimate at recommended defaults:** ~2× the #383 training cost (3 sources × 2 SDF cells × 2 LoRA ranks × 1 control = ~12 LoRAs vs #383's 72 — but documents are longer + the SDF+SFT-mixed cell from the original body adds one more cell tier). Concrete GPU-hour estimate goes in the plan.
